messages:
alex: quick standup — did: landed kernel prefetch patch (PR #842), ran kv warmup microbench across a small canary fleet, reproduced the high tail latency from last night; blockers: still seeing ~30ms tail on long-context workloads when microbatch merges occur (suspect slot stealing), need another eyeball on the slotting heuristic; today: finish profiler traces and open a followup PR to guard slot stealing, pinging @tess for review.

tess: thanks — can you paste the trace snippet? I can try to repro locally.

alex: trace excerpt pasted below, it's noisy but shows the spike around merge time:
```
kernel_loop: 1.2s
microbatch_queue -> merge_slots: 0.08s spike
kv.hit_ratio: 0.83 -> drops to 0.42 during merge
```
not exact timestamps (sanitized) but pattern is consistent.

maya: running dedicated-pool bench (3 runs) now, will share csv in ~45m.

sam: reviewed PR #842 — left a couple nits about comments and one question: did you test with batching_window=10ms? that parameter changed behavior in my sim.

alex: tested 10ms and 20ms; 10ms reduces avg latency but increases tail by ~8ms on long sequences. will attach raw bench numbers once maya posts them.

ops-bot: deploy started for canary group runtime-qa-003 at 1765433600 :rocket: (rolling, 3 nodes)

diego: quick thought — if we fast-fail slot grab when KV eviction > 75% (and fallback to smaller microbatch) does that help? I ran a quick sim and it cut the p99 spikes in half.

alex: yep, that's the guard I'm planning to prototype. will open PR after I finish adding traces.

tess: I can review the perf traces after the PR lands. also can we add a microbench that simulates LLM prefix cache churn? feels like our current microbench doesn't exercise that.

alex: agreed — adding a microbench ticket on the board: https://kanban/board/ENG-RUNTIME/PRJ-129 (will include churn patterns + varying batch windows).

maya: bench update (quick summary): configs: baseline / prefetch / prefetch+guard. p95: baseline=112ms, prefetch=95ms, prefetch+guard=82ms. p99 moves similarly. uploading CSV to the thread shortly.

sam: ping @alex for final review on the inline comments I left.

alex: on it, will address the comments today. thanks all :thumbsup:

buildbot: CI passed for PR #842 (master) — 12 tests, 0 failures.

tess: small nit — can we add a short comment in kernel_queue about expected microbatch ordering? otherwise LGTM.

alex: will add that comment and a tiny unit test for ordering. moving this to in-review. blockers mostly cleared for today but will keep monitoring the canary metrics.
